newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom leads New Zealand shares to a firmer close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom leads New Zealand shares to a firmer close.

text.p: * Telecom benefits from stronger bond market
New Zealand shares ended firmer on Wednesday, led higher by Telecom which benefited from a stronger bond market, brokers said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 13.75 points higher at 2,325.21, with Telecom up 10 cents at NZ$7.46.

Brokers said the U.S. debt market had taken heart before the close from opinion polls indicating President Bill Clinton would be re-elected, but that the Republicans would hold onto their Senate majority.
"New Zealand rallied on the back of that, and that would have helped Telecom," said Tim Koller at Hendry Hay McIntosh.

INL rose 12 cents to $7.15, its highest level since March, 1994. Brokers said investors who had sold their holdings in Wilson and Horton were moving those funds into INL to maintain their weightings in the sector.

Appliance manufacturer Fisher and Paykel, which today reported a $19.2 million profit for the six months to September 30, ended seven cents higher at $5.25. Brokers said the result was in line with expectations and the stock had been actively sought of late.
Brokers also noted a crossing of 1.5 million Fletcher Energy shares at $4.00/share. Energy ended three cents weaker at $4.00.
A 50 basis point rate cut in Australia had been well anticipated and had not affected New Zealand's equity market.
